verification.commit_state: working tree == doc-model commit; verification reflects exactly this state
verification.wiring: the whole document layer is consumed only by tests — no src/main/index.ts, preload or renderer import touches it yet (verified by grep). Nothing user-facing regresses; the bugs below are latent until M1.2 wires open/save.

blockers.title: readDeck throws (does not return an error value) on a manifest whose theme path is an Object.prototype key
blockers.detail: `entries[manifest.theme]` indexes the plain object returned by fflate's unzipSync with an attacker-chosen string. `manifest.theme` is only constrained by `isSafeArchivePath`, which accepts `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `__proto__`, etc. For theme="constructor" the lookup resolves up the prototype chain to `Object`, `themeBytes !== undefined` passes, and `strFromU8(Object)` throws `TypeError: The "list" argument must be an instance of SharedArrayBuffer, ArrayBuffer or ArrayBufferView`.
blockers.impact: Directly contradicts the module's own documented contract ("Never throws for bad input — errors are values", store.ts:89) and the §5.2 posture that a bad file yields a message, not a crash. Once File > Open is wired in M1.2 this is an unhandled rejection in the Electron main process on an untrusted .sloodge. Every later milestone stacks on this loader.
blockers.repro: pack a fixture, rewrite manifest.json with theme:'constructor', drop theme/theme.json, readDeck -> TypeError (reproduced)
blockers.fix: build `entries` lookups through `Object.hasOwn(entries, name)` (or copy into a null-prototype map / Map) before indexing; add a regression test for theme='constructor'.

majors.title: packDeck silently drops archive entries named after Object.prototype members
majors.detail: `claim()` guards with `if (name in zippable) return`. `in` walks the prototype chain, so extras named `toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty` are treated as already-present and never written. Reproduced: extras {toString, constructor, normal.bin} -> only normal.bin survives the round-trip.
majors.impact: Silent data loss that breaks the §5.2 guarantee this module advertises ("unknown entries are copied through verbatim"). Same root cause as B1; same one-line class of fix (`Object.hasOwn(zippable, name)` and/or `Object.create(null)`).

majors.title: No size or expansion-ratio cap on unzipSync — decompression bomb OOMs the main process
majors.detail: `readFile` is unbounded and `unzipSync` inflates every entry into memory with no total-size or per-entry limit. A few-hundred-KB crafted .sloodge expands to gigabytes.
majors.impact: .sloodge is explicitly designed to be emailed and double-clicked (§1). A malicious or merely corrupt deck hard-kills the app with no recoverable error. Add a max archive size, a max inflated total, and a max entry count, returning a DeckReadError code.

majors.title: Synchronous zip/unzip runs on the Electron main thread
majors.detail: readDeck/writeDeck are `async` but the actual work is fflate's *Sync* API. For a 100-200 slide deck with assets this blocks the main process — and therefore all IPC, the menu, and window responsiveness — for the whole read/write.
majors.impact: Guaranteed jank on open/save at realistic deck sizes. fflate ships `unzip`/`zip` (worker-backed) with the same options including per-entry `level: 0`; switching is mostly mechanical and much cheaper now than after M1.2-M1.4 stack on the sync signature.

majors.title: §2.2 invariant 4 is only 3/4 implemented, but the module header claims it in full
majors.detail: The spec's invariant 4 is "`..`, absolute paths, symlinks -> reject the file outright". `..`, absolute and drive-letter paths are handled; symlink entries (zip external attributes / unix mode) are not checked at all, and fflate's unzipSync does not surface them. Separately, the loop `if (name.endsWith('/')) continue` skips the safety check entirely for directory entries, so an entry literally named `../../evil/` passes the gate.
majors.impact: Harmless today because nothing is extracted to disk. §1.3 says an opened deck IS extracted to `userData/workspaces/<deckId>/` — at that point both gaps become live path-traversal. Either implement the symlink check and run directory names through `isSafeArchivePath` minus the trailing slash, or narrow the header comment and leave an explicit TODO tied to the extraction milestone.

majors.title: theme.json (§4.2) has no zod schema, and no milestone owns it
majors.detail: The PR is the project's designated 'zod schemas' PR, but the theme document is carried as opaque text. §4.2 specifies a full theme schema (formatVersion, t_ ULID id, mode, token colors with hex patterns, size ranges bound to SL-C*, series 3-8). `THEME_ID_PATTERN` is defined in types.ts and then never used. Grepping 80-roadmap.md, no later milestone mentions themes at all.
majors.impact: Not necessarily wrong to defer, but as written the theme schema is unowned work that will silently never land: a malformed theme.json will surface as a broken render in M1.3+ rather than a load-time error. Either add the schema here or file it against a named milestone.

items: No fsync of the containing directory after rename in writeDeck — the rename itself is not durable across power loss, though the file contents are.
Fixed `<path>.tmp` name means two concurrent saves to the same path corrupt each other; no lock.
`hasStaleTmp` is exported, untested, and unused — the §1.3 crash-recovery flow it exists for does not exist yet.
`options.id` is interpolated unescaped into `data-sl-slide="..."` in createStarterSlideHtml; SlideId is a bare string at the type level, so only convention prevents attribute injection.

Every schema is `z.looseObject`, so `SlideEntry`/`DeckManifest` carry an index signature and TypeScript's excess-property check is defeated — `updateSlide`'s `Omit<..., 'id'|'file'>` is enforced only at runtime (the test at deck.test.ts:199 relies on this), and field typos compile clean.
packDeck writes `bundle.slides[id] ?? ''` — a manifest entry with no HTML silently produces an empty slide file instead of an error.

readDeck/packDeck `continue` past `manifest.slides[id]` being undefined, and slidesInOrder skips missing entries; the schema makes these unreachable, so they mask invariant violations rather than surfacing them.
No `MIGRATIONS` chain / hook from §5.3 — correct for a v1-only build, but the extension point is absent, so v1->v2 will be a loader edit rather than an array append.
`newDeckId` and `newAssetId` return plain `string` and have no test asserting they match DECK_ID_PATTERN / ASSET_ID_PATTERN (only `newSlideId` is covered, indirectly).
Orphan `thumbs/<id>.webp` entries for deleted slides live in `extras` and are re-emitted forever; nothing garbage-collects them.

strengths: Schema is a faithful, well-annotated mirror of §2.2 including all four cross-field invariants; every deviation from the JSON Schema (constants instead of zod .default(), to keep parse->save byte-faithful) is explained in-comment.
Forward-compat is genuinely tested end-to-end: unknown manifest keys and unknown archive entries survive two full save/read cycles (store.test.ts:71-103).
format-too-new is probed before schema validation, so a v2 file yields the §5.2 'saved by a newer Sloodge' error rather than a wall of schema issues — and that ordering is tested.
Atomic-save failure paths are tested for real (rename-over-directory), including tmp cleanup and 'invalid manifest never touches the disk'.
mimetype-first-and-STORED is asserted at the byte level (local header offsets 8-9 and 26-27), not just via unzip.
deck.ts ops are genuinely immutable with explicit non-mutation assertions, which is the precondition M1.2's invert/undo layer needs.
The fflate-vs-jszip/adm-zip/yauzl choice is justified in-file against the concrete requirement (per-entry level:0 for OPC mimetype).
Starter slide is asserted against the actual Tier-1 lint rules it claims to satisfy, including the negative self-containment checks.

scope_check.not_delivered: theme.json schema (§4.2, see M5); migration chain (§5.3, vacuous at v1); no scope creep observed — no lint rules, no IPC, no UI
